$comment: SPEC-01, merging two design sections into one list (dev.md section 14 part 2: 'one vocabulary, spec/vocab/life-events.json, which also carries the adult-to-tell classes of section 13 so one list serves both'; the coherence review, question 1, confirms this over section 13's own earlier separate 'adult-to-tell.json' name). Two independent readers, one definition: `life_event` marks a class as consequential or unusually large news for computeFactConfidence() (CRED-01, dev.md section 14 part 2: a claim in one of these classes starts at confidence 0.50 rather than the ordinary 0.95, because a bigger claim needs more than one telling to firm up); `adult_to_tell` marks a class an adult tells a child in their own way rather than the hub reciting it (AGE-01, dev.md section 13 part 3: the deterministic, safe default that sets a household record's child_disclosure to adult_only at write time). A class may carry either flag, both, or - id present for completeness of the merge - neither meaningfully (every entry here has at least one). This list does not include the memory content policy's own sensitivity detector, which is dynamic and already flags other things independently; a class here is additional to that, not a replacement for it.

classes.description: Someone new joins the household, or someone leaves it.
The household, or a household member, is moving.
A separation or divorce, a household member's own or someone close to them.
A pregnancy, a household member's own or someone close to them.
A death, a household member's own loss or someone close to them.
A funeral or memorial, paired with death as one thing an adult tells a child in their own way.
A new diagnosis or a serious illness, a household member's own or someone close to them.
A new job, a job change, or a job loss.
A large, unusual purchase (a home, a car, something well above the household's ordinary spending).
A new pet joining the household.
An unusual financial gain (an inheritance, a prize, a large bonus).
A legal or police matter involving a household member.
An adult's own private plan (to leave, to move out, or similar) not yet acted on.
